pm_structure.summary: No external or affiliated asset manager is disclosed; ivari's general account appears to be run in-house under an ALM working group and Board Investment and Risk Committee, with a distinctive construct: ~C$3.6bn (32% of invested assets) sits in ETFs and mutual funds replicating universal-life policyholder fund options, hedged with equity-index and interest-rate futures; the C$6.0bn bond book is 90% >10-year, 34% government/provincial-heavy. Sagicor says ivari has 'margin expansion on investment portfolio' upside.

rotation_commentary.text: Sagicor flags 'margin expansion on investment portfolio' at ivari and says it is 'optimizing our balance sheet' in Canada (Q2 2026 call); core earnings up on higher expected investment earnings.
CEO acknowledged IFRS 17 market volatility is 'more pronounced' than big public peers and that curbing tails/hedging the investment program is under active board discussion.
Bonds fell to C$6.01bn from C$6.11bn (governments -C$215mm, corporates +C$91mm, energy +C$89mm) while ETFs/mutual funds rose to C$3.59bn from C$3.07bn; short-term up to C$1.30bn.
Sagicor group introduced an 'other financial invested assets' category for private debt and private equity; group private debt doubled to US$305mm.

notes: ivari is the largest Sagicor segment (US$11.5bn of US$25.1bn assets; ~73% of group core earnings) and the thinnest-capitalised name in the peer set (LICAT 129% Total / 98% Core). Balance sheet is distinctive: C$3.6bn of ETFs/mutual funds back UL policyholder funds, hedged with futures; a C$944mm funds-withheld reinsurance deposit accrues at 8.54% to 2077; bond book is long (90% >10y) and provincial-heavy. Parent leverage (27.4%) and financing (US$1.02bn notes/loans; C$350mm 2031 notes Sept 2026 via NBF/RBC) are the relevant funding story since ivari has no debt. All C$ figures from ivari's statutory FS; US$ figures from Sagicor MD&A.
